Your data belongs to you, and it stays that way. Uploaded files and prompts are never used to train any model — Caspr's included. Every analysis you run is retained in your account and is not used to improve the product for anyone else.

Caspr is built to ISO 27001:2022 information security standards and handles data in line with GDPR. Enterprise accounts add SSO for centralised authentication and admin-managed team controls, giving a security or procurement team a single point of control over who can get into the account and what they can do once inside.

Analyses are private to the account that runs them by default — team visibility is an Enterprise-tier setting, controlled by the account admin, not an automatic behaviour.

Talk to us about security.

By default, an analysis belongs only to the account that ran it. Nobody else — not a teammate, not an admin — sees it unless you choose to share it.

That changes at the Enterprise milestone. Research Budget is pooled across the team's three seats, and account admins get management controls over the team, including an optional per-seat spending sub-limit.

[VERIFY: confirm the exact default visibility rules at Enterprise — specifically what, if anything, an admin can see of a team member's individual analyses without an explicit share — before this answer is published.]

See account settings.

Enterprise accounts come with three seats by default, sharing a single pooled Research Budget of $1,800/month — roughly $1,674 of it available to spend on analyses across the whole team.

Any seat can run a Brief, Study, or Intelligence report; the cost draws from the shared pool rather than an individual allowance. The account admin can set an optional per-seat spending sub-limit to cap how much any one person draws down before the next billing cycle — the default is no limit, so the team simply shares the pool.

All billing runs through the admin's payment method. When someone leaves the team, their completed reports stay with the account while their access is revoked immediately. Talk to us about teams.

Yes. SSO is part of the Enterprise milestone — a $1,800/month Research Budget unlocks it alongside team seats and API access.

It's built for the procurement checklist as much as the security one: centralised authentication means IT controls who gets into the account, and deprovisioning happens at the identity layer rather than by chasing down individual logins when someone leaves. It ships bundled with the Enterprise tier, not sold as a standalone add-on.

For configuration details specific to your identity provider, talk to us about Enterprise.

Yes — API access is an Enterprise capability. A $1,800/month Research Budget unlocks it alongside SSO and team seats.

The intent is to let analyses be triggered programmatically — Briefs, Studies, and Intelligence reports — so Caspr can sit inside an existing research or reporting process rather than being a separate destination your team has to remember to visit.

Your account settings live in one place, split into a handful of clear screens rather than one long form. On mobile, the menu is flat: **Identity card · Research profile · Security · Notifications · Preferences · Sign out**.

**Identity card** holds your name, email, and the basics of who you are on the account.

**Research profile** is what Caspr has learned about you — role, interests, the kind of analyses you tend to run — gathered through short get-to-know questions inside Ask Caspr, folded directly into this screen rather than living separately. Every fact is listed in plain language, and you can remove any of them, or reset the whole profile in one action.

**Security** covers your password, two-factor authentication, and the devices currently signed in, with the option to sign any of them out remotely.

**Notifications** sets what Caspr emails or messages you about.

**Preferences** sets your defaults: language, output style, and format for new analyses. You can still override any of these per analysis at the gate, so Preferences is a starting point, not a lock.

Your spendable Research Budget, activity ledger, and invoices live in **Wallet** — on mobile, a primary bottom-nav tab of its own, not part of this menu.

Team visibility and seat management apply at the Enterprise milestone, where budget is pooled across seats and an admin can set per-user spending sub-limits.

Want a clean slate for one part of your account, or to close it entirely? The scoped resets — Research profile, Data Room, documents — each live on their own screen; Account's own danger zone holds only **Delete account**.

Open account settings.

Today, sharing a report means exporting it — download the PDF, or at Business the editable PPTX, and send it the way you'd send any file. Every citation travels with it, so a colleague can trace any number back to its source without needing their own Caspr account or logging into anything.

At the **Enterprise** milestone, sharing becomes structural rather than manual: Research Budget and seats are pooled, so every analysis run on the account belongs to the team, not just the person who ran it. Three seats are included by default, with an admin able to set per-user spending sub-limits if needed.

[VERIFY: exact in-app sharing mechanics — link sharing, view-only access for colleagues outside the seat count, or export-only — with the product team before publishing.]

For now, treat export as the reliable path: generate the format you need from the Outputs tab, in whatever language your recipient works in, and share the file directly.

Share your report.

Open your **Wallet** — it's the single screen for everything about what you have and what you've spent. On mobile, Wallet is a primary bottom-nav tab of its own, showing your live balance at a glance; Insights has moved into **More**.

At the top: your spendable Research Budget balance, the amount actually available to run analyses right now, shown to the cent (e.g. $186.00). Below it, an **activity ledger** — every analysis you've run, what it cost, and when, itemised individually rather than lumped into one monthly total. Run a Study and a Brief in the same week, and the ledger shows both, separately, at their fixed prices.

Your **next recharge** date and amount are shown too. Caspr recharges only what you spent the cycle before, so this number moves with your actual usage rather than sitting at a fixed monthly figure.

Invoices are downloadable directly from the ledger, one per billing cycle, ready for expensing or bookkeeping without digging through email.

One terminology note worth internalising: this is a **budget**, not a plan. There's no seat count to manage, no feature tier to remember — just a number you control and a balance that reflects exactly what you've used.

If your balance runs low, Wallet is also where you top up or raise your monthly budget.

Open your Wallet.

Caspr occasionally asks a short question inside the Ask Caspr thread — your role, the industries you follow, the kind of decisions your analyses tend to support. Nothing that blocks the report you're waiting on; answer it or skip it and keep going.

These get-to-know questions are the input; your **Research profile** is the output — a running record of what Caspr knows about you, used to fit future analyses to your actual work rather than starting from a generic template every time. Ask the same market-sizing question as a PE analyst and as a category manager, and the two reports come back differently scoped, in part because of what's in each profile.

Every fact Caspr has learned is listed on the Research profile screen, in plain language — nothing inferred silently and hidden from view. If something's wrong, outdated, or you'd simply rather Caspr forget it, remove it with one tap. There's no bulk reset required to correct a single fact.

Two things worth being clear on: answering these questions is entirely optional, and it never changes or blocks the report currently generating. The profile shapes future analyses, not the one already in progress.

Want a full clean slate instead of removing facts one at a time? **Reset research profile** clears every learned fact in one action, while keeping your account and Wallet balance intact.

Sharpen your profile.

Open **Preferences** from your account. It holds three defaults Caspr applies to every new analysis: your language, your output style, and your preferred format.

Set your language once — French, say — and every new report generates natively in French from the start, written that way, not English translated afterward. Output style governs how the report actually reads: vocabulary, chart treatment, appendices, overall length and density. Format sets which file type Caspr produces by default when a new analysis completes.

None of this locks you in per analysis. At the **gate**, before any specific report generates, you can override any of these defaults for that one run — send one analysis out in Spanish while your account default stays English, without touching Preferences at all.

Changing your defaults in Preferences doesn't reach back into reports already generated; it only applies going forward, from the next analysis you run.

Open Preferences.

Everything account security lives on one screen: **Security**, under your account settings.

**Password** — change it any time; you'll need your current password to confirm the change, standard practice against anyone who's gained partial access.

**Two-factor authentication** — enable it to add a second check on sign-in, beyond just your password. An authenticator app is the recommended method over SMS, which is more vulnerable to interception and SIM-swap attacks.

**Devices** — a list of everything currently signed in to your account. If you don't recognise one, or you've simply lost a laptop, sign it out from here directly, without needing to change your password first.

[VERIFY: exact two-factor methods offered (authenticator app, SMS, or both) and the specific device-list controls (per-device sign-out vs. a single "sign out everywhere") with the engineering team before publishing.]

The danger card at the bottom of Security holds one action only: **Delete account**. There's no separate account reset here — the scoped resets (Research profile, Data Room, documents) each live on their own screen.

None of this is optional friction — it's the same discipline you'd expect from any tool holding boardroom-sensitive analysis. Caspr is ISO 27001:2022 certified and GDPR compliant; account-level security is the layer you control directly, on top of that.

Open Security.

There's no single "Reset account" anymore. Instead, Caspr gives you three scoped resets, each living on its own screen, plus one account-level action that's genuinely final: **Delete account**.

**Delete account** is the only destructive action at the account level. It's final: your remaining Research Budget balance is **forfeited**, not refunded, and there's no walking it back once it's done. To confirm, you type the word DELETE — deliberately, so it can't happen from a stray click. Your data is retained afterward only as required for legal and GDPR obligations, not kept around for any other purpose.

Before reaching for that, consider whether one of the scoped resets gets you what you actually want:

- **Reset Research profile** — clears every fact Caspr has learned about you in one action. Your reports, Wallet balance, and account stay untouched.
- **Reset Data Room** — clears your uploaded files and Data Room settings without touching your account or your generated reports.
- **Delete all documents** — removes your generated reports while leaving your account, Wallet balance, and Research profile intact.

Each of these is reversible in the sense that your account keeps running afterward — you're clearing one part of it, not closing it down. Delete account is the one action that closes everything, and it's the only one that costs you your remaining balance.

If you're not sure which you want, start with the narrowest reset that solves the actual problem — a new client, a research focus that's drifted, a Data Room that needs clearing out — and treat Delete account as the last resort, not the default.

Manage your account.

Open **Get Help** from the navigation — on mobile, that means the **More** tab rather than a standalone bottom-nav destination. It's built as a searchable FAQ first, a message form second, because most answers don't need a person to deliver them.

Search directly for what you're stuck on, or browse by category: **Basics, Analyses, Pricing, Reports, Account**. Expand any answer inline, right where you found it — no separate page to load, no ticket to open for something the FAQ already covers.

If the FAQ genuinely doesn't answer it, use **Message support**. It pre-tags your message with whatever category you were browsing when you opened it, so support already has context before you've finished typing a word. Add a subject line, describe the issue, and send — no need to re-explain where in the product you ran into it.

[VERIFY: support response-time commitment before stating an SLA publicly.]

Get Help is designed so you don't need the exact right words for your problem. Search loosely, browse by category, or skip straight to messaging a person if you'd rather not hunt for the answer yourself. Most account and pricing questions are already answered inline — Message support exists for what's genuinely specific to you.

Open Get Help.
